title: Do the speaker's short underruns reach Moonlight?
hypothesis: The speaker's underruns of about 2 ms (lab 013) do not reach Moonlight: Sunshine captures Windows' mix before it goes to the speaker, so the sound on the host has no gaps or breaks that line up with them.

results.metric: gaps of 1 ms or more in the host's output (level under 30 % of the tone)
gaps of 1 ms or more in the host's output (level under 30 % of the tone)
breaks in the wave (sine predictor error)
results.notes: both at the two gaps, size 0.95 of the tone's peak; coding noise 4e-5

results.metric: breaks in the wave (sine predictor error)
speaker underruns heard (an event on the host within 150 ms of its expected arrival)
results.notes: underruns 0-6.2 ms; no event on the host without an underrun nearby

conclusion: Rejected: 2 of the speaker's 15 underruns in 10 minutes reached Moonlight as 9 ms gaps, and every event on the host lined up with an underrun; Steam Streaming Speakers had none in 5 minutes. They are short and rare (two clicks in ten minutes) but real. Next: complete each transfer a few milliseconds before its time so Windows sends the next one earlier; since Sunshine captures Windows' mix and not the speaker's output, this may not add latency, which a lab has to check.
